brief:
## The product: Classroom Widgets (by Tinkertanker, Singapore)
A teacher-facing toolkit of live classroom widgets — countdown Timer, Randomiser (name picker with confetti), Polls, Traffic Light, Task Cue, Volume monitor, QR code, Text banners, Sound effects, Stickers. Teachers arrange widgets on a canvas (web app) or, on desktop, launch them as floating always-on-top panels from a menu-bar / system-tray item. Vibe: warm, calm, playful-but-professional. Users are real teachers.

## Surfaces this ONE mark must serve
1. macOS app icon — 1024 squircle (plate rect x=100 y=100 w=824 h=824 rx=185; content may overhang the plate slightly but must stay inside the 1024 canvas).
2. Windows (.ico 16–256) and Linux (256 full-bleed rounded square) app icons — derived mechanically by scaling the squircle plate to fill the canvas, so the mark must survive full-bleed AND sit on light Windows Start / GNOME app grids (an off-white plate dissolves there).
3. Menu bar item (macOS template: single colour + alpha at ~18pt) and system tray (Windows ~16px WHITE on dark taskbar; GNOME symbolic white on black top bar) — currently a generic 3×3 dot grid; must be recognisably this app and NOT a generic grid.
4. Web favicon (16/32), PWA icon.

## Brand palette
Warm off-white plate #f3efe8→#dfeee8; sages #86b49f #7cb3a3 #5a9483 (a deeper sage ≈ #2f5646 / #3d6b58 is allowed so the brand owns one colour that clears 3:1); terracottas #d4775c #e89a80 #c25e42; dusty roses #d99185 #ebb4a9 #c8766a; cream #fdfcfb. The current icon is a calm 3×3 pastel grid.

## ROUND 2 — what round 1 taught us (nine evaluators, 81 verdicts; obey these)
- GLYPH FIRST. Draw the 16/18 px one-colour silhouette on the pixel grid before any colour. Minimum stroke 110 units, minimum gap/counter 100 units (≈2 device px at 16 px), closed-mass topology (one connected mass or two chunky masses — never scattered islands, hairlines or outlined boxes). Then grow the colour icon out of that silhouette.
- The outer silhouette must carry the identity: asymmetric, one memorable feature (a bite, a corner broken, an overhang). Marks inscribed in a plain circle or plain rounded box fail. No mirror symmetry.
- KILL ON SIGHT any silhouette that matches a system icon: clock/timer face, display/monitor, chat bubble, app-grid/launchpad, d-pad, record dot/target, copy-duplicate, wifi, gear, person/people. A small element floating OUTSIDE the top-right corner reads as a notification badge — avoid.
- Figure/ground by knockout and overlap, never by hue alone: sage vs terracotta is isoluminant (1.28:1) and vanishes in greyscale.
- Use all three brand hues (sage, terracotta, dusty rose) with intent; consider a SATURATED plate (deep sage or terracotta field with cream/pale figures) — the one full-bleed that held on the overview sheet was the saturated one.
- Plurality and liveness are missing: this is several widgets running at once. Where the direction allows, hint at more-than-one and at a running state.
- One consistent top-left light, soft warm shadows, no edge-parallel highlight bars, no ticks/pins/dots that die below 18 px.

## Non-negotiables
- Colour icon and monochrome glyph must be the SAME mark. Glyph: viewBox 0 0 1024 1024, fills only #000 (opacity 1; one 0.5-opacity tone allowed if essential), no gradients/filters; strokes only as stroke="#000" fill="none".
- Icon: viewBox 0 0 1024 1024, self-contained, ≤ 3 focal elements, survives 32 px, no text.
- CRITICAL: prefix EVERY id in the icon SVG with "{{SLUG}}-" and every id in the glyph SVG with "{{SLUG}}g-".
- Round-1 contact sheets you may Read for reference: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-classroom-widgets/1019d9be-4c14-5465-b2e2-1ffcd8946341/scratchpad/sheets/r1-<slug>.png for slugs lift, fan, orbit, bubble, dial, hand, board, mono, plus, and r1-overview.png.

directions.brief: Evolve round-1 'lift' (Read sheets/r1-lift.png). Panel consensus: the idea is the strongest in the set but socket and chip don't rhyme. FIX: the socket must be the exact footprint and corner radius of the lifted tile, cut from the slab's TRUE top-right corner (so the silhouette is a square with a corner cell missing); the chip overlaps that same corner on a ~14° diagonal with a directional shadow, breaking the slab's outline rather than floating outside it (no badge read, no copy-icon read). Hint the board with two faint seams (a 2×2) so 'board losing a tile' is legible. Shrink the slab ~12% for breathing room. Bring dusty rose in as a third hue (a seam or a half-visible tile). Glyph: same three parts, pixel-first, knockout ≥ 120 units.
directions.title: Lifted Tile — corrected (round-1 leader)

directions.brief: The same corrected lift geometry as 'lift2' but testing the saturated-plate rule: a deep sage field (#3d6b58→#2f5646 or the family's sage pushed to ~#4f8a74) with a CREAM board and the terracotta chip, so the full-bleed Windows/Linux/PWA tile has real edge contrast and the mark is ownable by colour. For the glyph, take the a11y panel's suggestion: the board as a thick outlined rounded rect (stroke ≥ 120 units) with the corner bitten out and ONLY the chip solid — about 35% ink so it matches system-glyph weight — provided the counter still holds at 16 px.
directions.title: Lifted Tile on a saturated plate

directions.brief: Evolve round-1 'fan' (Read sheets/r1-fan.png). Panel: charming, earns all three hues, but 18° fan flattens into three equal bars (equalizer / poker hand). FIX: landscape widget-card proportions, fan opened to 30–35°, front card visibly wider/shorter than the two behind, and the TOP card lifting out of the deck tilted (merge with lift) so the mark says 'take a tool from the kit'. Give the front card ONE abstract widget cue (a terracotta quarter-wedge or two poll bars) so it reads widgets, not cards. Glyph: union of the cards with ≥ 110-unit knockouts where they overlap; the fan angle and the lifted card must survive at 18 px as a single asymmetric mass.
directions.title: Deck of widgets — fan rebuilt and merged with lift

directions.brief: Evolve round-1 'orbit' by deleting the ring AND the centre dot (Read sheets/r1-orbit.png). Keep only three rounded tiles of three clearly different sizes in a loose, asymmetric, non-grid arrangement — one tilted — sage, terracotta and dusty rose (no honey). It should feel like widgets arranged live on a canvas. Glyph: the three solid tiles must touch or overlap into one or two connected masses (no scattered islands) with knockouts ≥ 110 units; the outer silhouette must be describable and not a triangle/trefoil/gear.
directions.title: Constellation — three unequal tiles, no ring

directions.brief: The liveness direction the panel asked for. ONE widget tile as the hero (rounded square, dominant), showing a running state: a terracotta countdown wedge sweeping around the tile's own rounded corner (the dial harvested as a detail, never a clock face), OR a poll bar half-filled. 'A widget that happens to be running', not a timer app. Consider a second, smaller tile tucked behind for plurality. Glyph: rounded square with the wedge as a KNOCKOUT (negative space) — a closed mass with one internal cut; no hub dot, no ticks, no full circle anywhere.
directions.title: A widget caught mid-run

directions.brief: The deliberately FLAT, hard-edged, two-colour treatment to break the uniform soft-3D rendering: a saturated terracotta (or deep sage) full plate with a cream 2×2 board knocked out of it as negative space, where one cell is missing — the mark IS the empty socket, with the missing tile shown small and tilted mid-air in the plate's colour. No gradients, no shadows (a single flat offset shadow allowed). Glyph: the same construction in black: solid board with one cell missing plus the tilted chip, all connected mass.
directions.title: Flat cut-out — the missing tile as the mark

directions.brief: The teacher lens: nothing in round 1 said 'a room with people'. A single widget tile (sage, dominant, maybe with a small terracotta wedge) held up above two or three round 'heads' (dusty rose / cream dots of different sizes) — the class looking up at the widget. Warm and human without drawing anatomy. Glyph: tile + two or three solid dots fused or with ≥ 100-unit gaps, forming an asymmetric mass; must NOT read as the 'people/group' or 'presentation' system icons — use unequal dot sizes and let the tile tilt.
directions.title: Widget facing the class

directions.brief: Round-1 'hand' was the bravest and the least legible (Read sheets/r1-hand.png). Rebuild it as the panel suggested: the TILE occupies ~60% of the mark and only an index fingertip and thumb-tip (two chunky rounded shapes, terracotta) grip its top-right corner; no palm, no wrist, no other fingers. The tile tilts ~12°. Glyph: tile solid + two fingertip shapes with ≥ 110-unit knockouts; if it cannot hold at 16 px, simplify to ONE fingertip touching the corner.
directions.title: Pinch — the hand reduced to two fingertips

directions.brief: Motion, not object: a single tilted terracotta tile at the end of a short, thick sweeping arc trail (sage) — a widget arriving onto the canvas. The arc is ~120–160°, not a ring; it starts thin-ish and thickens toward the tile, or fades via two stepped segments (no gradients in the glyph). Suggests the app's own loading/arrival animation. Glyph: thick arc (≥ 130 units) fused into the solid tile as one asymmetric mass; must not read as refresh/undo/loading spinner — keep the tile large and square, the arc short and heavy.
directions.title: Tile on an arc — motion as the mark
